name: Naduthariyappar Temple, Tirukandrapur (Kanrappur)
deity: Shiva as Naduthariyappar, with the goddess Srivalli Nayaki (Maathumai Nayaki)
period: Tevaram era (hymned 7th century); later Chola structural temple
summary: Kanrappur, the Tevaram's Tirukandrapur, near Tiruvarur, honours Shiva as Naduthariyappar with the goddess Srivalli Nayaki. A Paadal Petra Sthalam hymned by Appar, it is a quiet shrine of the Tiruvarur country, its name tied to a legend of the self-manifest lingam that would not be broken.

sections.history: Kanrappur, whose Tevaram name is Tirukandrapur, lies about 16–17 km from Tiruvarur in Tiruvarur district. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam, hymned in the Tevaram by Tirunavukkarasar (Appar). The spelling of the place varies across sources — Kanrappur, Kandrapur, Tirukkanraappur — and the stone temple is of the Chola period and later.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian delta temple, the shrine enshrines Naduthariyappar in the sanctum, with the goddess Srivalli Nayaki — also called Maathumai Nayaki and Madhumai Ammai — in her own shrine, a Nandi and the parivara devatas. The temple keeps the simple, well-ordered plan of the smaller Kaveri-country sanctuaries.
sections.legends: The lord's name Naduthariyappar (also Naduturaippar) is linked to a legend in which the swayambhu lingam, self-manifest from the earth, could not be cut or broken — when one tried to strike it with an axe, the lord stood firm and unharmed, and the place took its name from that steadfastness. The goddess's names, Srivalli Nayaki and Maathumai Nayaki, carry her gracious presence beside him. As with many smaller delta shrines, the fuller sthala purana survives chiefly in local tradition and Appar's verses.
sections.festivals: The temple observes Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship, at the quiet scale of a village shrine. Pilgrims on the Paadal Petra trail near Tiruvarur include Kanrappur among their stops.
sections.experience: At Kanrappur the pilgrim comes to a quiet shrine of the self-manifest lord who could not be broken. Before Naduthariyappar and Srivalli Nayaki, the visitor finds the steadfast grace of a Tevaram temple of the Tiruvarur country, firm as the lingam that rose from the earth.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Kanrappur is about 16–17 km from Tiruvarur, in Tiruvarur district. Tiruvarur is the nearest rail head, with town buses and taxis to the village.
